record.paper_title: Harvesting and stocking in discrete-time contest competition models with open problems and conjectures
record.original_question: For the delayed p-periodic stocking equation x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_{n-1}) + h_n, where h_n is a p-periodic nonnegative stocking sequence with positive total stocking over one period, a p-periodic solution exists and is known to be globally attracting when p = 2. Is that p-periodic solution globally attracting for every period p > 2?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the second-order difference equation with stocking
  x_{n+1} = x_n f(x_{n-1}) + h_n,  n = 0, 1, 2, ...,
where:
- f: [0, ∞) → (0, ∞) is a continuous, strictly decreasing function with lim_{x→∞} f(x) = 0 (so that x f(x) is a contest-competition recruitment function);
- the stocking sequence (h_n) is p-periodic and nonnegative with h_{n+p} = h_n for all n, and satisfies the positivity-of-total-stocking condition h_0 + h_1 + ... + h_{p-1} > 0;
- initial values x_{-1}, x_0 are nonnegative (and not both zero).

It is known that for every such system there exists a positive p-periodic solution, and that when p = 2 this p-periodic solution is globally attracting (i.e., every solution with positive initial data converges to it).

Question: For every integer p > 2, and for every choice of f and p-periodic nonnegative stocking sequence (h_n) as above, is the p-periodic solution of this equation globally attracting?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as a conjecture about delayed periodic stocking in discrete contest-competition models. A web search did not turn up any paper resolving the conjecture for general periods p > 2; related literature treats periodic Beverton–Holt and related models but not this specific delayed stocking conjecture. No evidence of resolution was found, so the status appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Periodic dynamics of a single-species population model based on the discrete Beverton-Holt equation
status_evidence.snippet: Results on existence and global attractivity of positive periodic solutions for periodic discrete population models, related but not addressing the delayed stocking conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on periodic discrete population models does not resolve the delayed-stocking global attractivity conjecture for p>2.
